data.name: Cynthia
data.gender_notes: Cynthia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'kynos', meaning 'dog' or 'hunter' and 'theia', meaning 'goddess'. In Greek mythology, Cynthia was a name given to the goddess Artemis, the huntress, protector of wild animals and the goddess of childbirth. The name Cynthia carries the meaning “Moon goddess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Cynthia usually hope their child will grow to embody moon goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Cynthia represents the feminine energies of the moon, intuition, and nurturing. It is a name for those who value the natural world and the cycles of life.
data.etymology: Cynthia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cynthia total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_greek.name: Κυνθία
in_greek.meaning: Αυτή είναι το φως, φωτεινή, πηγή φωτός
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κυνθία προέρχεται από το ελληνικό όνομα Κύνθος, που αναφέρεται στο όρος Κυνθος στην Κόρινθο. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα Κυνθία συνδέεται με το φως και την πηγή φωτός, συμβολίζοντας το divine φως και το φως του Χριστού. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα Κυνθία.

in_latin.name: Cynthia
in_latin.meaning: She is the light, shining, source of light
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Cynthia derives from the Greek name Κύνθος (Cynthus), referring to Mount Cynthus in Corinth. In Christian tradition, Cynthia is associated with light and illumination, symbolizing divine light and the light of Christ. Although not directly mentioned in the New Testament, the name Cynthia has been adopted in various Christian cultures.

in_english.name: Cynthia
in_english.meaning: She who is the source of light, shining bright
in_english.long_meaning: The name Cynthia originates from the Greek name Κύνθος (Cynthus), signifying 'mountain of light'. In Christian tradition, Cynthia represents illumination and divine radiance. The name Cynthia does not appear directly in the Bible but has been used in Christian communities to signify a person who embodies spiritual light and guidance. Historically, the name has been associated with purity, wisdom, and spiritual enlightenment.

data.cultural_impact: The name Cynthia carries a rich cultural heritage, particularly rooted in Greek mythology. As a Greek name, Cynthia holds an important place in history and literature, and it continues to inspire artists, writers, and filmmakers. It reminds us of the beauty, strength, and ageless wisdom represented by the mythological figure of the huntress goddess and inspires individuals with this name to embody the adventurous spirit and resilience of the ancient goddess.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, the name Cynthia can be seen as a reminder of the divine feminine energy that exists within all of us. It evokes the image of the powerful huntress goddess, who embodies the perfect balance between the wild, untamed aspects of nature and the nurturing, maternal forces of creation. For those named Cynthia, this name can serve as a source of inspiration and strength in honoring the divine feminine within and acknowledging the rich spiritual heritage from which this name originated.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Cynthia is derived from the Greek name 'Kynthia', meaning 'resembling Kynthos', the mountain of Delos where Apollo and Artemis were born. It symbolizes the balance between the masculine (Apollo) and feminine (Artemis) aspects of the divine, reflecting the harmony and wholeness within a woman.

historical_references.reference: Cynthia was an epithet given to the Greek goddess Artemis in Cyprus. The name comes from the Greek word kynos, meaning 'dog'. This name reflects Artemis' association with hunting and wild animals.

In early Christian Europe, Cynthia was adopted as a female given name. It is believed that the name was given in honour of the Virgin Mary, who was often referred to as the 'New Cynthia' due to her role as a protector of the faithful and her association with the moon.
